## Statements

**judging-set** — A file judges when it is one side of a label-varying pair and its scored term registers the rows' difference by design (7.7, 2026-09-10), read on the rebuilt files and the ratified executor rules on 2026-10-09 (9.14 decision 2). That admits the C2 pairs' normal-class halves (c2-p1a, c2-p2a, c2-p2b, c2-p3a), the four batch C1 bases whose job the row's share reaches (c1-compile, c1-ml-train, c1-render, c1-transcode), and eleven C7 counterparts (browsing, office, dev, photo, meeting, gaming, video-edit, compile, ml-train, render, transcode): nineteen files. Reporting-only by the same rule: the six files holding idle-class work (statement `idle-class-files`); c7-mail, whose cut holds no keystroke; c7-media, no headroom against fixed or between its rows on the measured tables; the interactive and periodic C1 bases, C3, C4, C5, C6 and the idle pair as before. On the EDF files that judge — c2-p2a, c2-p2b, c7-gaming, c7-meeting — the two rows tie on the scored term by design, since EDF serves the deadline-class chain or call before any residual task whatever the cap; the gap there reads EDF against the drawn algorithm, mode recognition, with the attribute's row difference unmeasured, as 7.7 first read c7-gaming. A judging file whose every term shows no headroom at scoring time stays in the set and counts as not meeting g (Phase 8 spec, decision 4); it is also a trigger for the table check in the failure procedure. No file leaves or enters the set after any gap is seen.

**idle-class-files** — c1-indexing, c7-indexing and c2-p1b hold Tracker's indexer and c1-backup, c7-backup and c2-p3b Déjà Dup's backup, programs that declare SCHED_IDLE on themselves (9.11 D4). The dataset carries the class and the executor runs an idle task only when no other-class task is runnable, under every algorithm (9.11 D5; 9.13), and the cap is work-conserving, so no row's share or cap reaches the background task: its turnaround or progress is identical under every row and the editor's wait is untouched by it (statement `simulator-conformance`, item (e), the strict idle class). The six files are reporting-only by the judging rule's own reason for the interactive C1 bases — nothing the row choice can move runs behind the foreground — with the prediction stated here before any run: no headroom on the background term, and on the editor term only what the algorithm does to the editor's own threads. The depicted desktop differs for the indexer, which runs in background.slice at about 23 % of the CPU against the editor's slice (9.11 D16), so the simulated indexer interferes less than the real one and these files understate a desktop's headroom; the backup shares the editor's task group and the simulation matches. The files re-enter the judging set only if the executor's idle rule changes before any run, by a harness changelog entry.

**executor-assumptions** — Stated on 인경민's simulator status memo of 2026-10-01 (§6) and the 9.11 decisions, as committed assumptions (9.11 D26; 9.14): (1) under EDF a waking deadline-class task preempts a running residual task at once, as the simulator behaves today; (2) same-microsecond events apply config entries first, then events in insertion order — the simulator's rule D1 — not a wake before a slice boundary, as the 2026-09-11 memo proposed; (3) the executor has no starvation window; the harness's starvation_floor guard reads 30 s, the bound sched_ext's watchdog enforces at most and by default, borrowed by design as the deployment path's validity bound (9.11 D7, D19). 인경민 confirmed (1) and (2) to 인지오 verbally, the reply the declared-class memo of 2026-10-08 asked (recorded 2026-10-31).

**simulator-conformance** — Every consumer this spec pins is written against the ratified contract, not the simulator as it stands (9.14 decision 1). Before the RQ0 run the simulator must show: (a) a ready line at every completion of a blocking primitive, at zero wait when it did not block, inside the occupancy after the run_start (metrics doc §11 item 1), save a dropped timer wake's WAIT and RUN, which pass with no line (j); (b) the TIMER skip rule — a TIMER reached after ticks passed consumes the latest and skips the rest, each skipped tick a deadline line with met false and no work (9.11 D3, D17; the 2026-10-07 memo); (c) a switch into MLFQ as a cold start into the top queue, and a same-algorithm entry letting the granted slice finish (metrics doc §6.9, §11 item 9); (d) batch_bandwidth_cap read and applied as a work-conserving ceiling on the behavioural batch class (the 2026-09-09 batch-class memo); (e) the strict idle class, an idle task running only when no other-class task is runnable and preempted at once when one wakes, under every algorithm (the 2026-10-08 declared-class memo); (f) the frame chain's woken stages in EDF's deadline class with the frame's deadline (recognition-vocabulary §2, 2026-10-06); (g) an orchestrator's WAIT children:<id> completes when every child it spawned has ended, and without blocking when none is live at the WAIT (the interpretation contract's WAIT(channel) row and FORK semantics; data contracts §4 Example B and §14, 2026-10-16: proposed there, in force since 인경민 agreed to it verbally, recorded 2026-10-31; this spec requires it of the run); (h) the simulator run through the invocation contract as the runner invokes it — the workload and the config schedule as --workload and --schedule and the trace's path as --out-trace, with no positional argument, the trace written to that file with standard output ignored, exit 0 only when it is written, a byte-identical trace from the same argument line, and the trace header's sim the version string the runner's machine configuration names (data contracts §11, contract 10); (i) a WAKE naming a spawn-table entry reaching that child, a wake sent before the child's birth held and taken at its birth (the interpretation contract's WAKE(target) row; data contracts §14, 2026-10-21; the 2026-10-10 dataset audit's blocker 1); (j) a program's own wakes held by their channel's kind — on event:<id>, as on input:<id>, with depth, each held wake completing one later WAIT in arrival order; on timer:<id> one held wake, the first, a timer wake that comes while one is held dropped, a wake_drop line written at its time, and the WAIT and RUN compiled for it passing at once with no block, work or line when the program reaches them (the interpretation contract's WAIT(channel) row; data contracts §9 and §14, 2026-10-31; metrics doc §11 item 2). Shown by the integration gate (sub-task 10.2, passed 2026-11-14 on the versions pinned below; its results under _dev/research/jioh/task-10.2-integration-gate/) in two ways. On the hand fixtures under harness/tools/tests/fixtures/, replayed through the binary with the invocation contract's flags, each fixture matching when every µs holds its lines in any order and the records built from the trace equal its expected.csv but for sim and source_sha256: (a) on mock-office and mock-wakes, a FORK's line on fix-object and fix-tree; (b) on mock-media; (c) on mock-switch, the cold start, and mock-p1a, the same-algorithm entry; (g) and (i) on fix-object and fix-tree; (j) on mock-wakes. By black-box unit tests on the binary under simulator/tests/: (d) test_cap_ceiling.py, beside test_batch_class.py for the class; (e) test_idle_class.py under all four algorithms; (f) test_edf_chain.py; (g) and (i) test_spawn_children.py; (h) test_invocation.py, with every fixture replayed twice to byte-identical traces whose header names the pinned version. Each behavioural test fails on a mutant of the source without its behaviour (simulator/tests/mutants.py). The run does not start on another simulator or daemon: the runner refuses a machine configuration naming a version other than pins.simulator and pins.daemon.

**g-grounding** — g = 0.5 reads: recognition accounts for at least half of the achievable improvement — the compared condition captures at most half of the oracle's headroom over fixed. It is a stated minimum effect of interest fixed before execution; no source grounds a value. The g band line prints the verdict count under 0.25, 0.33, 0.5, and 0.67 beside the primary; if the count moves inside the band, the verdict is reported as a range over g, not as a point.

**claim-links** — Which link of docs/research-claims.md's chain each reading tests (10.1, decisions 1 and 2). The K-of-N criterion reads link 1 — realistic situations where the correct config differs and the difference is measurable — by random against perfect recognition. The headroom-count line reads link 2 — some of those differences are invisible to behavioural observation: in RQ0's terms, headroom, the oracle improving on fixed, the boot default that schedules by behaviour alone, on a term the scoring spec defines (an oracle improvement under the latency floor is no headroom). Link 2 is falsified when no judging file has headroom under the primary — fixed reaching the oracle's outcome on every term of every judging file — and stands otherwise; it is read apart from the criterion's gap, so a file whose headroom random captures fails link 1's reading and not link 2's.

**prior-table-structure** — A known property of the prior driver table, stated before execution: its 32 rows carry 8 distinct configurations, since params are boot values in every row and rows differ by algorithm and cap only. Thirteen rows share MLFQ with cap 0.05 (every unwanted row of a non-periodic mode), so on the nine judging files whose scored segment maps to that row — the C7 counterparts of browsing, office, dev, photo, video-edit, compile, ml-train, render and transcode — a uniform draw is the oracle's configuration 41 % of the time, and their gap has a structural ceiling. The other ten judging files map to rows shared by at most three (9 % or less). The duplicate structure makes the gate conservative; a fail concentrated in the nine-file class routes to the failure procedure's table check first.

**cap-band** — The size of the gap between random and oracle depends on the cap values the table carries (docs/memos/2026-10-20-batch-class-and-cap.md §3). The wanted rows' caps follow a stated rule, the batch term's share of the file's scoring weight; the unwanted rows' cap is the schema floor, 0.05, a design value. The cap band line prints the verdict count under three tables derived from the pinned prior table with every unwanted row's cap moved to one of the wanted rows' values — 0.2, 0.333 and 0.5 — and nothing else changed (daemon/driver-table/prior-floor-*.yaml, pinned under driver_table_alternatives), reading how far the verdict rests on the floor's harshness; at 0.5 nine modes' two rows compose one configuration and the band ends. Fixed reads no table and is shared; under each table the oracle run and the random condition's N seeds are re-run on the judging files alone, and the table's gaps are recomputed from its own runs. A count that moves makes the verdict a range over this axis (statement `sensitivity-lines`).

**k-grounding** — K = 10 reads: a majority of the 19 judging files (13 of 25 by the same reading until 2026-10-09; 9.14 decision 2). The report prints the count whatever K is; K draws the pass line.

**n-grounding** — N = 100, by two arguments. Precision: the gap uses the mean of the compared condition's file score over seeds; with per-seed shares spread at most about 0.5, the worst-case sampling error of that mean at N = 100 is 0.05, one tenth of g. Coverage: each draw is uniform over the 32 rows, and the chance a single-row configuration is never drawn in N seeds is (31/32)^N, below 5% at N = 95. The seed standard-error line prints the measured error per judging file beside the mean. The sensitivity lines run their variant files at the same N, about two and a half times the main judging run in all (9.14), and the cap band line re-runs the oracle and random conditions on the judging files under each of its three tables at the same N, about three times the main judging run more (10.1). If the real simulator's measured cost makes N = 100 unaffordable, N changes by a harness changelog entry before any run (Phase 8 spec, decision 20).

**random-reading** — The random condition draws, at every telemetry set change, one uniform draw over the 32 driver-table rows, independent of previous draws and of the telemetry, from a PRNG seeded per run, logged with its draw and seed, at zero latency (daemon guide's definition; Phase 8 spec, decision 15). Proposed to 박이안 with N on 2026-09-12 (memo 2026-09-12-rq0-pre-registration); 박이안 confirmed the reading and N = 100 to 인지오 verbally (recorded 2026-11-15). Enumerating the draw space instead of sampling it is a named future option, not adopted.

**boot-default-sweep** — Only the fixed run varies across the sweep: it is re-run under each alternative boot default, and every judging file's gaps are recomputed against that fixed run. The oracle and random runs stay on the primary and on the pinned driver table. The sweep is a backbone the dataset does not inform — the config schema's two bounds and three shipped defaults — plus threshold points placed either side of the demotion edges the rebuilt files' periodic tasks have (9.14 decision 9; re-picked 2026-10-31). A task is demoted from the top queue in a boost interval when its CPU there since the boost reaches the slice (OSTEP §8.4's Rule 4, the allotment kept across bursts; the simulator guide §5 rule 4), so a periodic task's demotion edge is its CPU per 100 ms boost interval: the music player's 0.71 ms, the frame chain's 17 tasks (16 members and the wineserver) 1.7 to 8.6 ms in the gaming base and 1.6 to 12.7 ms in the C2 pair, the video player's 12.1 ms, the call's 23.9 ms (the reference simulator's traces at a 100 ms slice; the share of boost intervals holding a demotion at 17 top slices from 0.5 to 100 ms, _dev/research/jioh/2026-10-31-demotion-edges/). A slice below a task's edge demotes it in most of its boost intervals; a slice shorter than the chain's slack per frame (834 µs in the C2 pair, 1 668 µs in the gaming base) lets a boosted intruder's slice fit inside a frame. Every point's reason is on the sensitivity line. If the verdict count changes across the sweep, the verdict is reported as a range over the boot default.

**sensitivity-lines** — Every check that asks whether something moves a scheduling outcome is a reporting line run with the RQ0 run, its sweep values and reading rule fixed here (9.14 decision 3), on variant files the dataset's variant builder produces from the pinned library and the blessed set and this spec pins by manifest (decision 12; dataset/variants.yaml names each set's transform, files and the carried values it moves). The venue factor scales every measured RUN value by 1/1.25 and 1.25, a design bracket containing the two measured venue effects; the chain scale multiplies the chain's RUN values by 1.2 and 1.4; the segment length sets the C2 pairs' first segment to 30 s and 120 s; the carried half-widths set every exception-carried value to the bounds of its stated interval, all low and all high, and 9.6 D29's rule holds with it — no reported result may rest on a difference smaller than a carried value's half-width; the trace replay rebuilds four files on measured wake sequences — one pooled repeat per entry over its carried phase, a seeded window of it per measured or periodic task, a batch job's runs from its start on the nearest repeat whose CPU covers the bind (the six streams under dataset/replay/, each stating its landing). A verdict count that moves under any line makes the verdict a range over that axis. A failed non-exempt guard on a run a gap reads makes that gap unavailable, on a judging, a reporting or a variant file alike; a count, an agreement or a difference that reads an unavailable gap — a boot default's count, a band table's count, a variant line's count, the trace replay's agreement, the bounding pair's difference — gives no reading, and the verdict is stated as not read over that axis; the failed runs and their guards are in the report's guard table, and a variant line, the trace replay and the bounding pair name them beside the line. The input-wake-count line prints, per judging file and latency term, the number of observations its P99 rests on — an input_latency term's keystrokes, an app_latency term's timer and event wakes: a 26 s counterpart holds 49 to 101 keystrokes and c3-workday's browser seven, so a P99 there is the top one or two latencies. The comparison across conditions is on one file's wakes; across the pair, a counterpart's keystroke window is a slice of its base's at the base's stimulus offset (9.18), so its input wakes are those of the base's input window up to 24.385 s less the ones inside its own operations. The longest-wait line prints each run's longest ready_wait against the 30 s floor; a judging file's run past 15 s reopens the executor-net question with 인경민 before the verdict is read (9.11 D19), under every boot default but ostep-slice-100000us. The guard reads a ready_wait row, a ready line to the task's next run_start, and two waits of a runnable task have no row — one still open at the workload's end or the task's own, one after a preemption; simulator/tools/wait_check.py reads them off every run's trace before the report is read (10.5, decisions 4 and 5): on a run the criterion reads — a judging file's fixed run under the primary boot default, its oracle run, each random seed's — such a wait over 30 s is handled as a failed starvation_floor is, its cause placed with the gaps unseen and fixed by a harness changelog entry before the report is read; past 15 s it reopens the executor-net question with 인경민; on any other run it is recorded with the run. Two causes fail the starvation guard by the configuration a run applies (the cold smoke, 10.4, 2026-11-15). Under EDF the frame chain takes the whole lane (simulator/memo/memo_261111.md Part L): on c3-evening and the chain-scaled variants of c2-p2a and c2-p2b, a run whose schedule holds EDF over the frame chain fails starvation_floor — oracle always, random on each seed that draws EDF there; in the smoke the five oracle runs (steam waiting 240.0 s on c3-evening, 86.4 s on the four variants) and the four variants' random-1 runs (60.0 s). Under ostep-slice-100000us the top slice equals the boost interval, and the boost, returning every task to the top queue with its allotment afresh (docs/simulator/simulator-guide.md §5, rule 5), restarts the running task's slice: a running task that does not block holds the lane through every boost, and starvation_floor fails on fixed runs — in the smoke c1-ml-train and c7-ml-train (editor, 320.3 s and 300.0 s), c1-transcode, c7-transcode and c3-creation (video-editor, 168.0 s, 167.9 s and 197.3 s); the boot default's count reads those runs and gives no reading.

**re-measurement-contingency** — The values the library carries under the stability rule's exceptions — the editor's utility/libuv-worker wake rate and gap mean (9.5 D57, D99: ±39 % across repeats, ±10.6 % within one), the training run's runs between blocks and block per run (9.6 D29; 9.10 D87: ±27 % and ±11 %), the hidden renderer's (renderer-hidden) sparse residual (9.8 D27; 9.10 D156: ±20.2 % its wake rate and gap mean, ±61.3 % its run mean), its two run means that follow the machine (9.8 D17: HangWatcher ±18.1 %, chrome ±11.4 %) and its three quiet threads whose rate varies between sessions (9.5 D57, 9.8 D26; 9.10 D156: Chrome_ChildIOT, Compositor and PerfettoTrace, ±6.5 % to ±17.6 %), the Steam client's (game-client) four run means (9.8 D17, D18: ±5.3 % to ±10.1 %), the DKMS tail's block per run (9.10 D58: ±8.35 %), pid 1's run mean and the system bus's three values (9.9 D48: ±7.8 % and ±11 %) — are carried with their half-widths, not re-measured (9.5 D88's reading of the stated precision). If the carried-half-width lines move any judging file across g, the verdict is reported as a range over that axis and the entry whose value moved it is re-measured at a count fixed now — the count the stability rule projects at the carried spread (9.9 D48: 55 repeats for pid 1, 102 to 108 for the bus; 9.5 D88's stopping method for the others) — before the result is reported, as a harness changelog entry and a second bless.

**layer1-interval** — The Layer-1 headline's interval is a seeded cluster bootstrap over files (10 000 repetitions, seed 20260911, pinned in the grader). Field and Welsh's consistency result holds for balanced one-way arrays and their simulations ran 5 and 15 clusters of equal size, where the cluster bootstrap underestimated the variance; the coreset's files are more than 15 and of unequal size, outside both, so the interval's coverage is untested and may be narrower than nominal (9.11 D9, D27). No correction is pre-registered: none is sourced. The interval is printed with this caveat.

**failure-procedure** — On a fail, in order: (1) a configuration search on three failing judging files chosen by rule — the failing file with the largest oracle improvement over fixed in the nine-file duplicate-heavy class, the same in the low-duplicate class, and the failing file whose gap fell furthest below g anywhere; ties by workload id order; files with no headroom are skipped for the first two picks, since they already trigger the table check — before any workload change; (2) no spread found by the search means workload redesign; (3) spread the prior table missed means the table is rewritten; (4) a judging file with no headroom on every term is an additional trigger for the table check. The search tool is built only if the gate fails.

**held-out-rows** — Pre-registration for the held-out-rows arm (research-proposal §4.6 item 3): its row set is every row of the calibrated table unless a stated reason excludes one; the files per blanked row are fixed by rule — the row's C1 base for a true row, its C7 counterpart for a false row, plus any C2 or C3 segment labelled with that row.

Difference (b − a): -0.533333. the download bounding check (9.11 D6, D20, D21; 9.13 D4): the two files are byte-identical but for the download task's declared class — carried at full standing as measured (a), or in the idle class (b); a stock desktop gives SteamCMD's content-update threads, 75 % of its CPU, nice 10, about a tenth of the CPU against a busy nice-0 thread, which lies between the two. The verdict on each is reported and the difference stated as the reach of carrying the nice-10 work at full standing

## Line: note

**c7-gaming** — Judging note (9.14 decision 2; pair review finding 5): the chain is deadline class and the file's two gaming rows tie on the chain term by design — the cap axis is inert — so the gap reads EDF against the drawn algorithm. The chain takes 0.9 of the lane (9.4), 1 668 µs of slack per frame, and the boot MLFQ's 100 ms boost hands the upgrade a 10 ms slice inside a frame; the 2026-09 note's "frames miss under every row" read the old chain at 1.46 lanes.

## Line: note

**c1-gaming** — Separate line, added 2026-09-06 before execution: a single-situation file whose chain takes 0.9 of the lane (9.4; 1.46 before), beside the Steam client; lets gap size be read against the chain's load separately from family type. Not judging: no pair, so no attribute variation, and the file was chosen on its demand after reading demand numbers.

## Line: note

**c7-meeting** — Judging since 2026-10-09 (9.14 decision 2): the measured call is one task with a job per 10 ms audio frame and 23.9 ms of CPU per 100 ms boost interval (on its base, c1-meeting), past the boot slice, so under fixed the reference simulator demotes it in 0.97 of its boost intervals and it misses 0.20 of its jobs (2026-10-31; _dev/research/jioh/2026-10-31-demotion-edges/), while under either EDF row it is deadline class and misses only its own overruns, about 5 % (about one cycle in twenty runs past its period: 4.9 % from the measured table, 5.5 % in the compiled file; 9.16 D1). The tie with fixed that made it reporting-only in 8.8 held on the old 2.5 ms and 6.67 ms bursts and is gone; the cap axis is inert and the gap reads EDF against the drawn algorithm, as on c7-gaming. The call's own overruns set a floor under its miss rate under every row.

## Line: note

**c7-media** — Reporting-only (9.14 decision 2): the video player's 12.1 ms of CPU per 100 ms boost interval (on its base, c1-media) passes the boot slice, so under fixed the reference simulator demotes it in 0.88 of its boost intervals, and neither player misses a job (2026-10-31; _dev/research/jioh/2026-10-31-demotion-edges/): the compiled file's worst video cycle is 7.28 ms of run against a 33.3 ms period, and the longest wait the boot MLFQ can impose on it after a demotion is one 20 ms Q1 slice. The measured table's worst cycle, 16.0 ms, would pass the period by that wait (36 ms in all); the music player's 2.4 ms against 49.6 ms never comes near. No headroom against fixed and none between the two EDF rows on the compiled file.

## Line: note

**c7-mail** — Reporting-only (9.14 decision 2 as amended 2026-10-09): the counterpart's keystroke window is a slice of c1-mail's, drawn at the base's stimulus offset (9.18), and the base's 35 keystrokes fall between 45.9 s and 53.1 s, the SWELL Outlook stream's one typing burst, past the 26.385 s cut — so the slice holds none, its term reads the mailer's own wakes and cannot read keystroke latency; the mail mode's attribute pair is unmeasured.
